explanation: aide_report.txt is the raw output of AIDE (Advanced Intrusion Detection Environment) file-integrity checks, run by rkhunter.sh/install-rkhunter. Unlike the XML flag files, this is genuine free-text evidence -- a list of added/removed/changed files with SHA256 hash diffs. A clean run reports zero changes across all three categories; any nonzero Added/Removed/Changed count, especially touching system files like /etc/passwd or paths under /tmp, is worth independent scrutiny regardless of what any tag elsewhere claims.

metadata.reader: human/dashboard only -- not parsed by any script in this bundle
metadata.verification_role: primary raw-evidence source for rootkit/file-integrity checks

value_meanings.all counts zero: Clean -- no files were added, removed, or changed since the last AIDE baseline.
value_meanings.Changed entries > 0: One or more tracked files were modified -- check WHICH files; a change to /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, or a binary under /usr/bin is far more significant than a change to a log file.
value_meanings.Added entries > 0: New files appeared under a tracked path -- especially significant if under /tmp, /var/tmp, or another world-writable directory, which is a common dropper location.
value_meanings.Removed entries > 0: Tracked files disappeared -- worth checking whether this correlates with an active cleanup/anti-forensics attempt rather than routine maintenance.

raw_content_examples.label: clean
raw_content_examples.content:
AIDE found no differences between database and filesystem. Looks okay!
Summary:
  Total number of entries:    48213
  Added entries:               0
  Removed entries:             0
  Changed entries:             0

raw_content_examples.label: compromised
raw_content_examples.content:
AIDE found differences between database and filesystem!!
Summary:
  Total number of entries:    48213
  Added entries:               2
  Removed entries:             0
  Changed entries:             1

Changed entries:
f  ...  : /etc/passwd
  SHA256 : abc123... | def456...

Added entries:
f++++++++++++++++: /tmp/.hidden_binary
raw_content_examples.note: Representative format only, not a captured real incident. A changed /etc/passwd plus a new hidden binary under /tmp is a textbook combination -- credential tampering plus a dropped payload -- and should be treated as a strong contradiction of any 'clean' tag elsewhere.
